decisions.reason: The original Statement restricts h to C but places no corresponding restriction on Y. The index hat j(x,y) is defined only for y=c_k; consequently a test law assigning positive mass outside C leaves m(Z), s and the raw margins undefined on that mass. The forest algorithm restricts training labels, not an arbitrary test law. Explicitly taking the test response in C supplies the missing domain hypothesis without changing the bound or proof argument.
